thread:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — while validating variant fallbacks for EU, I hit a tokenizer/tool-call parity issue when falling back to the small-quantized variant in eu-west1. Tool-calls are failing on some prompts with attachments.
Priya Rao: ugh. can you paste an example? is it only EU or other regions too?
Alex Chen: example below. request routed to model: redwood-small-q4 followed by fallback to redwood-base. The tokenizer splits a tool call token differently so the tool parsing fails.
Alex Chen: ```
input: "CALL_TOOL:convert_currency{"amount":100,"from":"USD","to":"EUR"}"
expected tokens: ["CALL_TOOL", ":", "convert_currency", "{", "amount", ...]
actual tokens (small-q4): ["CALL", "_TOOL", ":", "convert_currency", ...]
```
Jamie Park: that underscore split is nasty. could be a subword vocab mismatch from quantized model's tokenizer config.
Carlos M.: do we have a compatibility matrix that tracks tokenizer vocab/merges per variant? we need it surfaced in console before rollout.
Sasha I.: we have a matrix CSV but it's not exposed in console. it's under infra/compat/token_matrix.csv and it's stale.
Tina: telemetry shows ~0.4% toolcall errors spike in eu-west1 during the last canary. here's the query I ran: `SELECT count(*) FROM logs WHERE error_type='tool_call_parse' AND region='eu-west1' AND ts>now()-1d` — result 342.
Alex Chen: can we add a fast gating rule in routing to prefer non-quantized fallback for customers in higher tiers (dedicated/reserved) until we verify parity?
Priya Rao: routing rules already support tier-based weights, but not parity-aware preference. That's the convo we had last week.
Jamie Park: internal API debate: do we add a boolean `require_tool_parity=true` on the route config, or bake parity checks into the routing policy engine? I'm leaning toward the route-level flag for rollout agility.
Carlos M.: route-level flag sounds simpler. need UI/console UX: toggle with warning and link to compat matrix + test prompt set.
Sasha I.: good call. we'll need a background job to run the test prompt sets per variant and report pass/fail. where to store results? suggestions?
Tina: store in telemetry as per-route metrics + a dashboard tile. we can extend existing per-route/model dashboard with a 'compatibility score' panel.
Alex Chen: also quota implications — if we route from small-q4 to base and token counts change, customers might hit quotas unexpectedly. need to add an alert and soft quota buffer.
Priya Rao: yep. add a flag `quota_stability_margin_pct` on rollout policy. default 10%.
Jamie Park: implementation plan: (1) add `require_tool_parity` boolean to route config + console toggle; (2) background parity runner that posts results to telemetry and CEP (console endpoint); (3) routing engine checks parity flag and prefers compatible variants; (4) add quota margin and alerting.
Carlos M.: I'll spin up a quick compatibility suite with about 120 toolcall prompts across languages. can we gate EU rollouts with it?
Sasha I.: infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/compat-runner -> staging at 2024-06-08T03:00Z :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: canary started for compat-runner (run id: cr-20240608-1)
Tina: action items: assign ticket RW-4242 to eng-platform for route flag + console UX; RW-4243 to eng-ml for parity runner; RW-4244 to eng-telemetry for dashboard.
Alex Chen: thanks. small ask — can we also annotate fallbacks in logs with the variant pairing so it's easier to query e.g., `fallback_from=redwood-small-q4 fallback_to=redwood-base` ?
Jamie Park: agreed. cheap change, will add structured fields in logs.
Priya Rao: can someone add a short blurb in the rollout docs about tokenizer parity risk and recommended test prompt sets? I'll draft it.
Carlos M.: I'll start the prompt suite and run locally. will update RW-4243 with initial pass/fail matrix.
Sasha I.: moving to implement route-level flag; will aim for PR by EOD tomorrow.
Tina: thx all. note: if any enterprise customers are affected ping success@redwood and legal depending on data residency concerns.
Alex Chen: closing loop — once we have the dashboard tile and fail counts, we can throttle fallbacks automatically based on error rate. follow-up meeting next Tue 10am.
